- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.00) in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% relative to prior day’s forecast.
- After a recent spike in price, model often overshoots and forecasts too high for the next 3–5 days; apply a 5–10% downward bias to early forecast points post-spike.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.20 or higher), model tends to overestimate near-term prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 1–3 of the horizon.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if price is above 65, forecast tends to drop; if below 60, tends to rise — apply a 1–2% adjustment toward historical mean (avg of last 5 days) for mid-to-late horizon.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), model is prone to flat forecasting; introduce 0.5–1.0% volatility adjustment to forecast to reflect market uncertainty.
